fatal_errors: The proposed PtPdRhRuIrOs ethanol-oxidation system does not match the target Pd@PtRuFeCoNi shell studied for HER and HOR.

It predicts that annealing-induced ordering improves activity, whereas the target attributes high activity and durability to the kinetically trapped, randomly mixed shell; ordering and phase separation occur only upon elevated-temperature treatment.
No prior evidence is supplied for the asserted ordering-to-ethanol-oxidation causal relationship.
Annealing can simultaneously change particle size, surface composition, segregation, strain, and support interactions, so the proposed comparison does not isolate atomic ordering.
The falsification rule incorrectly treats failure to produce a structural change as falsification of the mechanism rather than failure of the intervention.
explanation: The hypothesis is internally testable at a basic level and uses an appropriate unannealed baseline, but it reconstructs neither the material architecture nor the reactions, controls, active sites, and adsorption mechanism in the target. The only partial overlap is the use of heating to alter local order and the generic idea that electronic structure affects adsorption. In the target, however, heating was a phase-stability probe: the random PtRuFeCoNi shell persists through 200°C, orders at 300–400°C, and phase-separates at 500°C. Catalytic superiority was instead linked to near-thermoneutral hydrogen adsorption, Ru-centered HER chemistry, potential-dependent Pt/Co/Ni behavior during HOR, and low-temperature kinetic stabilization. The suggested experiment would be more discriminating with particle-size- and surface-composition-matched controls, direct quantification of ordering, operando intermediate measurements, and a falsification criterion conditioned on successful induction of ordering.
